rows.name: TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT
rows.values: Whole number `0` or larger, digits only, parsed with `std::from_chars`. A value above `16` is lowered to `16`. Any other text, also empty text, aborts the process.
rows.default: Unset: 8 pieces. Empty: the value is invalid and the process aborts.
rows.effect: Sets the largest number of pieces into which TRON splits the software attention work on one KV cache page (64 tokens). Different attention workers (CPU threads that compute software attention) can then run the pieces. `0` or `1` turns splitting off.
rows.notes: The attention worker count also limits the pieces. Work for fewer than 32 tokens computed together is not split. A bad value aborts at the first forward pass with software attention work, not at startup. No flag exists. No log line shows the value.

evidence.quote: "invalid TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT '{}'; expected a nonnegative integer", value);

rows.name: TRON_ATTN_STATS
rows.values: Exactly `1` turns the statistics on. Any other text, also empty text, leaves them off and logs one warning per process.
rows.default: Unset: off, and no message is logged. Empty: off, and one warning is logged.
rows.effect: Turns on the attention path statistics. They count the attention work on 3 paths: the AVX loop and the AMX kernel on the CPU, and the FPGA cards. Lines that start with `[attn-stats]` go to stderr when a model state (the run-time object of a loaded model) is destroyed.
rows.notes: No flag exists. When on, the info log shows `attention path stats on (TRON_ATTN_STATS=1) for model`. The FUSE stats file `/model/<model id>/attention/summary` shows `"on":true`. Per-layer and per-worker files exist only when on. The stderr lines appear only when work was counted. `README.stats.md` describes the output.

evidence.quote: "TRON_ATTN_STATS='{}' ignored: exactly \"1\" turns the attention path stats on",
"attention path stats on (TRON_ATTN_STATS=1) for model '{}'{}: rows for "

rows.name: TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR
rows.values: Decimal number, parsed with `std::stof`. Text after the number is ignored. A value below `1.0` counts as `1.0`. Text with no leading number ends the process at first use.
rows.default: Unset: a factor of `2.0`. Empty: `std::stof` throws, and the process ends at first use.
rows.effect: When a sequence outgrows its KV book (a block of KV cache memory for a run of tokens), the scheduler requests a new book. The requested size is the page capacity of the old book times this factor, rounded up to whole pages of 64 tokens.
rows.notes: `TRON_BOOK_MAX_TOKENS` caps the result. At the root of the token tree (the scheduler's tree of all token sequences) and one node below it, `TRON_BOOK_INITIAL_TOKENS` sets the size instead. First use is the first book growth, not startup. No flag exists. No log line shows it.

rows.name: TRON_BOOK_INITIAL_TOKENS
rows.values: Integer number of tokens, parsed with `std::atoi`. A result below `1` counts as `1`. Text that is not a number counts as `1`.
rows.default: Unset: 1600 tokens (25 pages of 64 tokens). Empty: 1 token, which is rounded up to 1 page.
rows.effect: Sets the preferred size of a new KV book (a block of KV cache memory for a run of tokens). It applies to tokens added at the root of the token tree (the scheduler's tree of all token sequences) or one node below it. Sizes round up to whole pages.
rows.notes: `TRON_BOOK_MAX_TOKENS` caps this size. A value above that cap has no effect. A book is still made large enough for the tokens being added. Other new books start at 1 page or grow by `TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR`. No flag exists. No log line shows the value.

rows.name: TRON_BOOK_MAX_TOKENS
rows.values: Integer number of tokens, parsed with `std::atoi`. A result below `1` counts as `1`. Text that is not a number counts as `1`.
rows.default: Unset: 1600 tokens (25 pages of 64 tokens). Empty: 1 token, which is rounded up to 1 page.
rows.effect: Caps the size that the scheduler prefers for a new KV book (a block of KV cache memory for a run of tokens). The cap is rounded up to whole pages of 64 tokens. The request is raised above the cap when the added tokens need more pages.
rows.notes: It caps `TRON_BOOK_INITIAL_TOKENS` and the result of `TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR`. The value is read once per process. A wrong value logs no message. No flag exists. No log line shows the value.

rows.name: TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `std::atoi`. It counts nodes of the token tree (the scheduler's tree of all token sequences). `0` and text that is not a number mean off.
rows.default: Unset: `0`, which turns book defragmentation off.
rows.effect: With a value N above `0`, the scheduler tries to merge KV books (blocks of KV cache memory, one per run of tokens) before it adds tokens to a sequence. For the extended tree node and up to N-1 ancestors, a book moves into its parent's book when it fits.
rows.notes: A negative number becomes a very large depth and ends the process during a later generation. With `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH` above `1`, program start logs the warning `Fragmentation Risk!` when this value is below `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH`. No flag exists. No log line shows the value.

evidence.quote: return env ? std::atoi(env) : 0;  // Disabled by default.

rows.name: TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH
rows.values: Integer number of tree levels, parsed with `std::atoi`. The root counts as level 1. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. `0` and `1` draft no token.
rows.default: Unset: 2 levels. Empty: counts as `0`. No token is drafted then.
rows.effect: Sets the largest depth of the draft tree. In speculative decoding, a draft model proposes this tree of candidate tokens, and the main model then verifies them. A draft step adds one level only while the tree is shallower than this value.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when speculative decoding is active (see `TRON_USE_SPECULATION`). With the default `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE` of 2 nodes, a depth above 2 levels adds no verified token. A negative number becomes a very large limit. No flag exists. No log line shows the value.

rows.name: TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE
rows.values: Integer number of tree nodes, the root included, parsed with `std::atoi`. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. `0` aborts the process during speculative decoding.
rows.default: Unset: 2 nodes. Empty: counts as `0`. The process aborts during speculative decoding.
rows.effect: Sets the largest number of nodes kept in the draft tree. In speculative decoding, a draft model proposes this tree of candidate tokens, and the main model then verifies them. The tree is reduced to this size before each extension step and before verification, leaves first.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when speculative decoding is active (see `TRON_USE_SPECULATION`). With the default, only the root and 1 drafted node reach verification. A negative number turns the size limit off. No flag exists. No log line shows the value.

rows.name: TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH
rows.values: Integer count of new leaves per draft step, parsed with `std::atoi`. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. `0` drafts no token. A negative number is not rejected.
rows.default: Unset: 1 leaf per draft step. Empty: counts as `0`. No token is drafted then.
rows.effect: Sets the largest number of new leaves that one draft step adds to the draft tree. In speculative decoding, a draft model proposes this tree of candidate tokens, and the main model then verifies them. The count covers one whole tree level.
rows.notes: Drafting uses it only in speculative decoding (see `TRON_USE_SPECULATION`). With a value above `1`, program start logs the warning `Fragmentation Risk!` when `TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH` is below `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH`. With the default `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE` of 2 nodes, a width above 1 leaf adds no verified token. No flag exists.

rows.name: TRON_FIRST_RESULT_WARMUP
rows.values: Exactly `0` skips the warm-up. Any other text, also empty text, leaves the warm-up on. No message is logged for other text.
rows.effect: With `0`, startup skips the first-result warm-up. The warm-up runs one discarded matrix multiply with int4 (4-bit integer) weights on each FPGA card with PCI device id `0x0011` or higher. A source comment says that the first int4 result after an FPGA configuration is wrong on some bitfiles.
rows.notes: The info log shows `INIT: first-result warm-up skipped (TRON_FIRST_RESULT_WARMUP=0)` or `INIT: first-result warm-up: one int4 matmul on each of`. The same comment says that the warm-up clears the fault. The tests `t_first_result_fault` and `t_newregs` set `0`. `rinzler_proxy` does not read it. No flag exists.

evidence.quote: // On some Archer bitfiles, the first type-0 (int4) weight fetch after an FPGA

rows.name: TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS
rows.values: Path of a JSON file. The file is an array of token ids, or an object that maps a prompt key (comma-separated token ids) or `default` to tokens to emit.
rows.default: Unset: an error is logged, and every generation fails with `proxy: golden map unavailable`. Empty: the same failure, with the cause `cannot open TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS file`.
rows.effect: Names the file from which `rinzler_proxy` takes the tokens that it emits in place of running a model. The variable and the file are read again for every generation. A changed file takes effect at the next request.
rows.notes: An unreadable, non-JSON or wrongly shaped file fails every generation the same way. The process keeps running. A file with `rendered_at` needs `RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE` with the same text. Each generation logs `proxy: prompt key <key> -> <N> golden tokens`. `README.proxy.md` describes the format.

rows.name: TRON_HEAP_PROFILE_PATH
rows.values: Path of a file. The file is opened in append mode with `std::fopen`.
rows.default: Unset: no profile is written. Empty: counts as a path. The open fails and a warning is logged.
rows.effect: When an allocation from the hugepage heap fails for lack of memory, the arena allocator (`pos_heap_v2`, the build-default allocator of that heap) appends a histogram of the live allocations to this file. The histogram is grouped by size class and by caller address. Each block starts with `=== OOM n_live=`.
rows.notes: A profile is written only when the arena allocator is in use and its shadow map (per-allocation tracking) is on: `TRON_HEAP_SHADOW=1` or `--heap-shadow`. The info log line `pos_heap_setup: using arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) with shadow map` confirms both. A failed open logs `heap_v2::dump_profile: could not open`.

new_terms.definition: A block of KV cache memory that holds a run of consecutive tokens. Its size is a whole number of pages. One page holds 64 tokens.
The tree in which the scheduler stores all token sequences. Sequences that start with the same tokens share nodes.
A generation mode in which a draft model (EAGLE) proposes the next tokens and the main model verifies them in one batch.
The tree of candidate tokens that speculative decoding builds before the main model verifies them. The root is the last sampled token.
The run-time object of one loaded model. runtron builds one model state per prompt batch.
The two CPU code paths of software attention. Each is named after the CPU instruction set that it uses.
A CPU thread that computes software attention.
The heap allocator `pos_heap_v2` for the hugepage heap. It is the build default. `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` selects it at run time.
A record of the size and the caller address of every live allocation. The arena allocator keeps it when `TRON_HEAP_SHADOW=1` or `--heap-shadow` is given.
One discarded int4 matrix multiply that the FPGA driver runs on each FPGA card at startup.

notes: All 12 rows were checked against the source at commit 7eddde7895. No row is dropped. Every evidence quote of the first version matched its source line. Corrections of meaning: TRON_BOOK_INITIAL_TOKENS applies at the tree root and one node below it, whatever the token count of that node. TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR is not used there. The FPGA counters of TRON_ATTN_STATS are per layer only. TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH runs per scheduler step, not per HTTP request, and only one file contains its name. The draft tree rows now state that a larger depth or width adds no verified token while TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE has its default of 2 nodes. Decisions kept from the first version: TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS has for=developers and topic=generation. TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH and the three TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_* rows have for=operators, as the input records say. No code comment settles these two choices. Two results come from reading the code and the C++ standard, not from a run: a negative TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH and non-numeric TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR text end the process. The term golden file is removed from new_terms. No cell uses it. The term int4 is added. Line 3224 of h/tron/models/model.hpp proves the 0, 1 and 32 limits of TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT, but it holds a pipe character, so it is not quoted.

changes.name: TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE
changes.was: Sets the largest number of nodes kept in the draft tree (the tree of candidate tokens that speculative decoding builds before the main model verifies them). The tree is pruned to this size before each extension step and before verification. Pruning removes leaves first.
changes.now: Sets the largest number of nodes kept in the draft tree. In speculative decoding, a draft model proposes this tree of candidate tokens, and the main model then verifies them. The tree is reduced to this size before each extension step and before verification, leaves first.
changes.why: The cell used the term speculative decoding without a definition, and the uncommon word pruned. The code facts are the same (src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:278-321, :622, :695).

changes.name: TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE
changes.was: It has an effect only when speculative decoding is active (see `TRON_USE_SPECULATION`). `0` fails `TRON_ASSERT(max_nodes > 0)` at the first prune. With the default, at most the root and 1 drafted node reach verification. A negative number turns pruning off. No flag exists.

changes.why: No log line prints the value, and the cell now says so. The assert text is dropped from prose (it is in the evidence, src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:290).

changes.name: TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH

With a value above `1`, program start logs the warning `Fragmentation Risk!` when `TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH` is below `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH`. Verification keeps at most `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE` nodes. No flag exists.
